Lazarus. A friend of Jesus from the village of Bethany near Jerusalem, who lived with his brother Martha and his sister Mary. He died and was buried while Jesus was away, his body in a tomb for four days before Jesus's arrival. Jesus raised him from the dead in one of the most dramatic miracles in the New Testament. In the famous moment, Jesus cried out "Lazarus, come out!"—one of scripture's most dramatic sentences. He emerged from the tomb still bound in burial cloths, requiring others to unbind him, symbolizing incomplete resurrection until the Resurrection itself. This public miracle was a defining sign of Jesus's divine power and the fulfillment of resurrection themes, and it became a turning point in the Gospels, intensifying both belief and opposition to Jesus. After witnessing this extraordinary display of power, the chief priests plotted to kill both Jesus and Lazarus. His story appears in the Gospel of John as a climactic sign before Jesus's own Passion and Resurrection.
